resources.string: Switch the second SIM slot between your stored eSIMs with one tap in Quick Settings. Your main SIM (data and calls) stays on.
This app needs Shizuku, a free app that lends other apps the rights of a USB debugging session without root. Install it, start it (Shizuku → Start via Wireless debugging), then come back.
Shizuku isn\'t running. Open it and start it via Wireless debugging. It stops after every reboot; Shizuku can start itself on a trusted Wi-Fi (see its settings).
Shizuku is too old, please update it.
Allow eSIM Tiles to use Shizuku.
No stored eSIM profiles are visible. On this phone the system doesn\'t give them to Shizuku, so the app can\'t help here.
The SIM for data and calls. The app never switches it off.
Your main SIM is off or gone. Turn it on in Settings → SIMs, or pick another one here. Until then the tiles won\'t switch.
Pick up to %1$d eSIMs. Each gets its own tile; a tap puts it into the second slot instead of the one there now.

How it works: the app only enables profiles that are already on the phone; it never deletes or downloads anything. It has no internet access and doesn\'t read your messages. After a switch it puts data, calls and texts back on the SIMs you had them on. Switching takes about 15 seconds; ask for an SMS code only after the SIM shows signal.

Switching turns off the eSIM that is in the second slot now. Calls and texts to that number won\'t reach you until you switch back. The app uses hidden Android functions: on some phones it may not work or may behave unexpectedly. Make sure you know how to turn a SIM on in Settings → SIMs.
The phone wants you to confirm the switch: open eSIM Tiles.
Couldn\'t show the confirmation: %1$s. Use Settings → SIMs.
Copy report for a bug report
Report copied. It has no phone numbers or SIM serials.
Didn\'t switch: the phone returned an error (%1$d/%2$d).
The phone reported success, but the SIM isn\'t on. Check Settings → SIMs.
